## What changed

**Nothing was changed on this task, because the optimizer never saw it.** The N=30 pilot's `val` split contained 2 tasks (`traces_parsec-aap2-0047` and `-0048`); this is one of the other 28. It has exactly one measurement in the whole experiment: a single trial in the reference sweep.

## What worked

N/A — nothing was attempted.

## What didn't

The contract is defective. `tests/expected.json` lists **zero** assertions, and an empty list scores `assertions: 1.0` vacuously. Combined with `trajectory: 0.000` over 9 demanded calls, that produces a baseline of exactly **0.500** in which the agent demonstrably earned nothing: it did not reproduce the tool sequence, and there was no answer requirement for it to satisfy or miss.

And it could not have reproduced the sequence in any case. This task's contract demands **9 tool calls** in a `subset` match, including `db_describe_table` and `query_provisions_db` — none of which any simulator running on 2026-08-12 exposed. One uncallable op fails the whole ordered containment, so **trajectory 1.0 was unreachable here by construction**, and half of this task's reward was never in play. Across v1 trajectory scored 1.0 on 5/5 tasks whose demanded sequence was fully callable and 0/25 of those that were not.

## What we can (or can't) learn

**Nothing about the skill, and this row should not be in a mean.** It is the clearest single instance of the v1 benchmark's real problem: the contracts were extracted from traces mechanically and not reviewed, so a task can score 0.500 without measuring anything. Sum this task into a 30-task average and it drags the headline **up**. It is the only such task in v1 (traces_parsec-aap2-0052), which is why it is flagged on the row rather than dropped — dropping it silently would be the same class of error in the other direction.
